New Step 2b (was not one of the original 4 steps): points to the C2 proposal now specified in the ledger doc. Step 5: baseline row rewritten to record the decided shape.

3. docs/design/UI2_0_D1_OPTION_A_CONSOLIDATED_REVIEW.md (new) -- primary review entry point. One row per council finding (8 total) naming its resolution and exact location; a change log for both sibling documents; fail-closed/no-device-contact reaffirmation (the append-only reconciliation model is strictly STRONGER on tamper-evidence than the original draft's option, not weaker); validation summary; residual open items.

(a) The proposed 15-minute connectivity freshness bound (finding 7) is a concrete number for confirmation, not a claimed-uniquely-correct value -- no precedent number exists anywhere else in the repository for this "bounded window" language, for backup or restore.

(c) console/app.py's action_class_level wire field inventory (finding 1) is scoped to what this repository's own source can confirm; it cannot rule out an external client parsing that field as a strict integer.
(d) Both sibling documents still require nexus-decision-council review (GOV_PO_ROLE_MIGRATION.md section 7 trigger b) from a nexus-po PLAN/DECIDE episode before either may move from DRAFT to FROZEN -- this consolidation prepares them to be reviewed together in one round, it does not substitute for that round.
(e) Per-vendor restore_push gate-registry rows (the actual ten-field gate entry) remain out of scope, named but not specified, for whenever a concrete restore capability is authored.
(f) Both this commit (339d964) and the earlier one (5492960) sit on branch ozandur-garanti-cautious-waffle, not on this relay file's own worktree/branch -- a future integration step must bring both commits' files onto whichever branch the successor amendment movement actually lands on.

entries.text: Product Owner clarification supersedes the engineer's proposed fixed 15-minute freshness value (docs/design/RESTORE_CONTROLLED_WRITE_LEDGER.md section 3.3, first revision): do not freeze 15 minutes or any other fixed number. Revise the DRAFT contract bundle (docs only, no source/tests/frozen contract) to model freshness as configurable policy, explicitly separating background polling cadence from claim-time restore safety. Specify alternatives: (1) mandatory claim-time active connectivity/protocol probe as the authoritative path; (2) cached telemetry/SNMP as an optional lower-load evidence source only when its configurable TTL, identity binding, freshness, and semantic sufficiency are met; otherwise fail closed and perform active probe. Do not claim SNMP proves write-channel readiness unless a vendor-specific contract establishes it. Include policy fields, min/max/default bounds as proposals (not frozen), precedence, stale/unknown behavior, and audit fields. Incorporate the already-selected C2/C7 direction (relay seq 9): fold new admission facts into C7's existing check 1/check 2 model, not a separate check 7. Add a concise research note that BackBox public docs show pre-restore availability/credential checks and backup integrity verification, but do not use vendor product behavior as neXus authority.

Completed the revision per relay seq 13 (narrowly supersedes seq 9). Committed as b0be28a on branch ozandur-garanti-cautious-waffle (sibling worktree to this relay file's own -- same caveat as prior commits 5492960/339d964/9dbd3d0: not on this branch, not pushed, no PR).

CORE DECISION IMPLEMENTED: an explicit restore-ledger reconciliation-pending check now exists at C2 claim time, fail-closed, repurposing C2 section 6's existing check-4 slot (currently stated NOT_APPLICABLE for restore -- now reads "for controlled-restore-write jobs: this ledger's own check; NOT_APPLICABLE for every other class, unchanged"). Zero new rows in C2's table -- honors seq 9's original "no separate check 7" preference in letter, while satisfying seq 13's requirement in substance that this fact cannot remain compile-time-only. C4 static sign-off remains fully independent of C2 runtime admission throughout (section 3.0 explicitly reaffirms this, unreopened).

WHAT CHANGED (3 docs/design/*.md files revised, no source/test/FROZEN-contract/project-state file touched):

1. docs/design/RESTORE_CONTROLLED_WRITE_LEDGER.md -- section 3.1 rewritten into a two-tier model: C7 section 5.3 checks 1/2 stay an early, non-authoritative compile-time pass (unchanged from the seq-9 fold); C2 section 6 check 4's slot becomes the authoritative claim-time check. New section 3.1.0 states the compile-time-vs-claim-time distinction explicitly as its own subsection, with a table showing both dispositions for each fact -- addresses the "make C7 check mapping explicit" and "clarify compile vs claim" council findings directly. New section 3.1.1 DEFINES THE EXACT KEY/SCOPE: device_id stays the primary key (unchanged from the prior pass's resolution); ClusterXL cluster members are naturally independent by construction, since each member is already its own device_id per C4 section 4.2/4.3 -- no new mechanism needed, though whether one member's restore can leave the OTHER member's state uncertain is named as an open item cross-referenced to C7's own already-open section 9.8 ("multi-member consistency-group restore is not fully worked out"), not invented an answer for here. VSX: one physical device_id hosts multiple virtual_system_ref contexts; the conservative default keeps device_id-WIDE scoping (a reconciliation-pending state on one virtual system blocks restores to every virtual system on that same physical box) -- a narrower per-virtual-system alternative requires its own council-reviewed, per-vendor/platform contract (mirroring the semantic-sufficiency contract mechanism), none of which exists today. New section 3.1.2 DEFINES RESTORE_RUN/STEP CARDINALITY: one ledger "attempt" entry per restore_run (C2 job), never per individual device-write step within that run -- matches C7's own job-level (not step-level) OUTCOME_UNKNOWN handling exactly; record_attempt's docstring is corrected (previously wrongly said "once per restore-write step"). New section 3.1.3 DEFINES RETRY BEHAVIOR: a job BLOCKED at claim by this check never reached EXECUTING and remains ordinarily re-claimable on a future cycle -- explicitly distinguished from the class's own never-auto-retry rule (section 3.4), which governs a CLAIMED/EXECUTING job's failure, a genuinely different event.

Further council findings addressed this pass: section 3.3.1's semantic-sufficiency contract reference is now keyed per (vendor, platform_role_scope) rather than a single global flag, mirroring C4's own gate-registry key shape, and every entry must itself pass GOV_PO_ROLE_MIGRATION.md section 7 trigger (b) council review before being added -- no entry exists today for any vendor/platform. Section 6 (retention/privacy) is rewritten to state the append-only invariant WITHOUT QUALIFICATION, explicitly retracting a stale "one narrow, audited exception" hedge that had outlived its own resolution in an earlier pass. Section 7 is retitled and rewritten to state the full C7/C2 check mapping in one place. Sections 8/9/10 updated with new test obligations (staleness-between-compile-and-claim, restore_run cardinality, BLOCKED-vs-no-retry distinction, VSX/ClusterXL scoping) and restructured open items.

2. docs/design/UI2_0_D1_OPTION_A_AMENDMENT_PROPOSAL_BUNDLE.md -- Step 2's "necessary, never sufficient" paragraph and Step 2b (retitled again) rewritten to state the two-tier model and the check-4-slot repurposing in full, replacing the withdrawn single-fold description. Step 5's baseline row updated to record the decided shape across relay seq 5/7/9/13 plus the freshness clarification.

3. docs/design/UI2_0_D1_OPTION_A_CONSOLIDATED_REVIEW.md -- five new finding rows (9-14) covering: compile-vs-claim distinction, VSX/ClusterXL key/scope, restore_run cardinality, retry behavior, and keyed semantic-sufficiency contracts + append-only unambiguous restatement. Finding 4/5 rows revised to record this pass's supersession honestly (three revisions total, none silently overwritten). Fail-closed reaffirmation extended: the explicit claim-time check is named as a THIRD place this revision strengthens fail-closed behavior -- it closes a real gap the prior compile-time-only model left open (a plan compiled against a clean target, then claimed after a NEW unreconciled outcome appeared in the interim, would have been silently admitted under the old model; it is now refused fresh at claim).

(a) The check-1/check-2 compile-time mapping (which check absorbs "no unreconciled prior outcome" as an early pass) remains this document's own proposal -- check 5 is a plausible alternative; the claim-time check-4-slot placement is the seq-13-mandated, settled part.
(b) VSX device_id-wide scoping is a conservative default, not a settled per-vendor answer -- narrower scoping needs its own council-reviewed contract, none exists.
(c) ClusterXL cross-member risk (whether restoring one member can leave the other's state uncertain) is NOT answered by this ledger's per-member-independent scope -- cross-referenced to C7's own open section 9.8, not resolved here.
(d) Whether a perpetually-BLOCKED job should auto-expire is a generic C2 job-lifecycle question, not decided.
(e) All three documents still require nexus-decision-council review before any may freeze.

entries.text: Product Owner review decision: continue with the current physical-device restore model. Repository evidence confirms backup_assignment and backup_artefact are device/endpoint scoped; CP Gaia backup collection is not valid inside a VSX virtual-system context, and no current restore capability targets an individual VS. Therefore do not frame the current contract as a VSX per-virtual-system restore admission problem. Revise the three DRAFT docs so: (1) current restore/ledger scope is physical device_id/endpoint_id; (2) VSX virtual_system_ref restore is explicitly UNSUPPORTED/blocked/not in current scope; (3) any future VSX-context restore requires a separate vendor/platform and target-scope contract; (4) retain ClusterXL member identity separation only where relevant to future physical-member capabilities. Also prepare the explicit C7 5.3 companion amendment resolving the contradiction: class 1 retains the existing cadence-ledger interpretation, class 1.5 uses the restore reconciliation ledger, and other classes remain NOT_APPLICABLE. This is a review/correction decision on the engineer's own prior draft text (which had wrongly framed VSX scoping as an open admission-policy choice), not a new architectural decision -- it corrects the record against evidence already present in this repository's own frozen contracts. Do not freeze, implement, push, or open a PR.
